title: worktree-compose configuration
description: Configuration for wtc (worktree-compose), read from .wtcrc.json or the "wtc" key of package.json in the main worktree.

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference for editor completion. Ignored by wtc.

sync.description: Extra repo-relative files or directories copied from the main worktree into each worktree on start. Entries that are absolute or escape the repository are skipped.

envFile.description: Env filename copied from the main worktree and injected with ports (root and selected workspaces). Must be a bare filename.

workspaces.description: Monorepo workspaces (package name, directory name, or repo-relative path) that also receive env copies and port injection.

envOverrides.description: Extra variables written to the root env file. Values interpolate ${VAR} with allocated port variables and ${COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME}.

workspaceEnvOverrides.description: Per-workspace variables, keyed by workspace package name, directory basename, or path. Same interpolation as envOverrides.

portStride.description: Allocated port = 20000 + default port + worktree index × portStride. Raise it (e.g. 100) when default host ports are clustered.

composeCommand.description: Which compose tool to use instead of auto-detection (docker compose → podman compose → docker-compose → podman-compose; the first whose daemon answers wins). Repository config may only choose one of these four, so a cloned repository cannot make wtc run an arbitrary program. For a custom command (an absolute path, global flags such as --context, nerdctl, …) set the WTC_COMPOSE_COMMAND environment variable, which takes precedence.
